epic.title: Vertical Integration Inward — recombine DPF's own functionality into one legible shape
epic.description:
Home for the two merged UX-refactor design specs and the work behind them:

- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-14-portfolio-shaped-information-architecture-design.md` — reconcile the six rail sections toward the four FPAW portfolios (PR #4311, amended #4355/#4495)
- `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-interaction-shape-graph-and-design-shaping-design.md` — a machine-checkable model of the intended human-interaction shape, with fitness-function enforcement (PR #4312, amended #4355/#4495)

**Governing idea.** The complexity of getting work done — services, models, tools, adapters, agents — is real and must stay hidden. The shape is the far simpler figure a human traverses over the top of it. The two are coupled, not fused: the graph knows the machinery, the user sees their job.

**The one hard boundary.** Hiding machinery must never soften the vocabulary that carries the enterprise guarantee. `GAID`, `AIDoc`, `TAK-JSI qualification`, assurance claim, chain of custody, action receipt and clearance are standard-bearing terms from the platform's own normative corpus — they are taught, not hidden. An AI coworker *has* an agent identity; the two are different objects. Sorting vocabulary by how technical it sounds rather than by what it names is the failure mode this epic exists to prevent (see §3.4 of the shape spec).

**ID note.** Created with an auto-generated id because `EP-8DC217EB` is absent here. If that epic later arrives via a recovery bundle from another installation, reconcile the two rather than running both — this epic is the same initiative under a different id.
epic.scopeRationale: Governs the interaction shape, navigation taxonomy and user-visible vocabulary of every portal surface across all archetypes; the per-org nuance is inherited from the existing archetype value-stream projection rather than modelled per organization.

items.title: Measure setup cost: `prerequisitesToEntry` flow-load metric and the `entry-gated-by-setup` finding
items.body:
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-interaction-shape-graph-and-design-shaping-design.md` §3.3, §4, §10 phase 2, §11 (merged in PR #4495).

**What.** Add a fifth flow-load metric and its finding:
- `prerequisitesToEntry` — configuration, connection, or permission steps standing between stated intent and the first `entry` node of a job path.
- `entry-gated-by-setup` — fires when a job path's entry requires configuration that could have been requested in-flow, at the step that needs it.

**Why.** All four existing metrics (`stepsToOutcome`, `sectionCrossings`, `groupExits`, `deadEnds`) begin at `entry`. Setup cost is therefore invisible by construction: a job fronted by connector configuration scores identically to one that starts on first intent. That gap is where a non-technical operator abandons — before ever reaching a surface the current model would score as healthy.

**Composes with existing work.** The Connections cockpit (§4.5 of the companion IA spec, `BI-2A0180A9`, PR #4380) is the concrete remedy: *"the coworker detects a missing connection mid-task and requests + provisions it in the conversation … so the surface is the fallback, not the default."* The two were authored independently and agree — this BI supplies the measurement, that one supplies the mechanism. Link them on triage.

**Acceptance.**
- Every job path reports `prerequisitesToEntry`, so setup cost is visible rather than invisible-by-construction.
- `entry-gated-by-setup` fires on a path whose entry is fronted by configuration that could be requested in-flow.
- Budgeted and ratcheted like the other flow-load metrics (advisory for pre-existing, blocking for net-new).

**Epic.** Spec names `EP-8DC217EB`, which is not present in this installation's backlog — link on triage.
items.scopeRationale: Adds a metric to the platform-wide UX flow-load budget applied across all routes and archetypes; not customer-business logic.

items.title: Add `delegate` to the shape-graph stepRole set before the flow-load baseline is written
items.body:
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-interaction-shape-graph-and-design-shaping-design.md` §3.2, §4, §11 (merged in PR #4495).

**What.** Add `delegate` to the closed `stepRole` set, which is currently `entry · progress · decide · complete · reference`. A `delegate` node is a surface where the human hands the remainder of a job to an AI coworker. It terminates the human's traversal for flow-load purposes, and its `continuesTo` names the receiving `jobLane` rather than another surface.

**Why this is a modelling defect, not an enhancement.** Without `delegate`, a delegation surface types as `progress` or `decide`, so handing work to a coworker *increases* `stepsToOutcome`. The flow-load metric would then penalise the platform's primary answer to cognitive load — the reduction-gear / chief-of-staff pattern.

**Ordering constraint (load-bearing).** This is phase-0 contract work. If phase 2 writes the flow-load baseline first, the baseline bakes in the inverted metric and every later delegation surface scores as a regression. Cheap now, expensive after the baseline exists.

**Acceptance.**
- `delegate` is in the `stepRole` closed set and the extractor emits it.
- A `delegate` node does not increase `stepsToOutcome`; the count stops at the delegation.
- Delegated work remains subject to `spine-stage-inert`, so a stage cannot look cheap by delegating work that never completes.

**Epic.** The spec names `EP-8DC217EB` (Vertical Integration Inward) as its proposed epic home. That epic is not present in this installation's backlog — link on triage if it exists elsewhere or is created here.
items.scopeRationale: Extends the platform-wide interaction shape-graph node contract; applies to every human-reachable surface across all archetypes, not to one organization's business logic.

items.title: `spine-stage-inert`: detect a value-stream stage that is fully traversable but produces nothing a human accepted
items.body:
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-interaction-shape-graph-and-design-shaping-design.md` §3.3, §10 phase 3b, §11 (merged in PR #4495).

**What.** Add the `spine-stage-inert` conformance finding: a stage is bound to surfaces and fully traversable, but no job path reached a `complete` node on it within the observation window. Requires per-stage completion observation over a rolling window.

**Why.** The existing checks certify that a flow *can* run. None checks that it *did*. A stage can bind cleanly, hold no dead ends, pass every page budget, and still produce nothing a human accepted. `spine-stage-orphaned` already applies this inverse logic to *missing* shape; this extends it to *inert* shape.

This is the platform's answer to the sharpest criticism of agent products generally — that activity gets mistaken for value. Without it, the conformance suite certifies process and is silent on outcome, which is the dimension an enterprise buyer actually evaluates.

**Interaction with `delegate` (BI-5A1A3C13).** Delegated work stays subject to this finding, so a stage cannot be made to look cheap by handing work to a coworker that never completes.

**Acceptance.**
- Per-stage completion is observed over a rolling window and surfaced as a finding, not only as a metric.
- A bound, traversable, budget-passing stage with zero completions in the window is reported.
- Rendered on the shape lens alongside the other findings (phase 4).

**Epic.** Spec names `EP-8DC217EB`, which is not present in this installation's backlog — link on triage.
items.scopeRationale: Observes completion across the operational value-stream projection for every organization and archetype; the detector is universal platform substrate over per-org data.

items.title: Three-class lexicon for the shape graph: hide implementation detail, teach the GAID/TAK standards corpus
items.body:
Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-15-interaction-shape-graph-and-design-shaping-design.md` §3.2 (`lexicon` field), §3.3 (`lexicon-leak`, `guarantee-unnamed`), §3.4, §9, §10 phase 2b (merged in PR #4495).

**What.** Add the `lexicon` field to the shape node contract and implement the two checks it governs. Terms sort by what they NAME, not by how technical they sound:

| Class | Rule | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Implementation detail | Hide | `capsule`, `extractor`, `projection`, `decomposition`, `pregate`, `backlog item`, `epic` |
| Operator vocabulary | Use | the words already in `page-purpose.job` / `successOutcome` |
| Standard-bearing | **Teach** | `GAID`, `Agent Identity Document`/`AIDoc`, `TAK-JSI qualification`, assurance claim, chain of custody, action receipt, clearance |

**Why the third class exists.** An AI coworker *has* an agent identity — two objects, not two names for one. GAID (`docs/architecture/GAID.md`) is a normative published standard alongside TAK and TAK-JSI, each with a conformance-test suite. That vocabulary is the evidence a coworker is attributable and governable, which is what an enterprise is buying. A binary "operator words good, technical words bad" rule would soften it away and delete the guarantee. The first draft of §3.4 made exactly that error; it was corrected in #4495 after operator review.

**Two findings.**
- `lexicon-leak` — a user-visible string names an implementation detail.
- `guarantee-unnamed` — a surface performs a governed action *without* naming the guarantee behind it. This is the inverse check that protects the corpus from the ease-of-use push.

**Mechanism (no new machinery).** `ux-route-sweep` already drives every route in a real portal and already captures an ARIA snapshot, so the visible strings are in hand at sweep time. Grade and ratchet exactly as §5 grades everything else: pre-existing baselined and improving-only, net-new blocking.

**Hard constraint.** The standard-bearing list must be DERIVED from the normative corpus (`docs/architecture/GAID.md`, the TAK / TAK-JSI standards and their conformance tests), never hand-maintained. A second glossary is drift by construction and violates single-source-of-truth.

**Ordering.** The `lexicon` field is phase-0 contract work; the checks are phase 2b. A baseline written before the field exists has no record of which leaks were pre-existing.

**Evidence the problem is real and currently unenforced.** Retiring one leaked primitive — `WorkCapsule` → `Workroom` — took four coordinated PRs (#4338, #4339, #4340, #4342) plus a database model rename.

**Epic.** Spec names `EP-8DC217EB`, which is not present in this installation's backlog — link on triage.
items.scopeRationale: Governs user-visible vocabulary across every portal surface and every archetype, and binds to the platform's own normative standards corpus (GAID/TAK/TAK-JSI); not customer-business logic.
